thesis: The strongest bear case is not solvency but scale and reinvestment: roughly $359B of cash/T-bills can depress returns if Abel cannot find sufficiently large opportunities. Insurance catastrophe, falling short rates, capital-intensive BHE/BNSF and acquisition integration can reduce normalized per-share growth. None currently meets a Hard Veto definition.

evidence.claim: Cash/T-bills were $359.2B, indicating enormous dry powder but also an opportunity-cost burden.
H1 capex was $10.6B and BNSF/BHE expected another $8.6B for the rest of 2026.
2026 acquisitions include OxyChem ~$9.4B and Taylor Morrison ~$6.8B.
Insurance investment income fell to $5.738B H1 2026 from $6.260B H1 2025.

counterevidence: Liquidity is exceptionally strong and repurchases are disciplined.
unknowns: Catastrophe tail correlation with equity-market losses.
Long-run T-bill allocation if rates normalize.
falsifiers: Three-year per-share operating earnings growth falls below inflation.
Insurance float cost rises while investment income falls.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 경영진 정직성 또는 회계 신뢰성 훼손
hard_veto_flags.rationale: No qualifying integrity/accounting reliability event identified.
External financing is not structurally required for operations.
Mature profitable businesses disprove customer-value absence.
No evidence incremental ROIC is structurally below cost of capital.
No persistent consolidated moat contraction is established.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 현재가격이 비현실적인 Bull Case 이상을 요구
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Current price is below modeled Bull value.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 단일 제품·단일 고객·단일 규제에 대한 치명적 종속성
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Diversification prevents fatal single product/customer/regulation dependence.
